question.text: Why does FATF recommend that countries have measures to detect the physical cross-border transportation of currency and bearer negotiable instruments?

answer.text: Because physical movement of cash and bearer instruments is one of the primary methods criminals use to move illicit value across borders, bypassing the formal financial system
Because FATF wants to eliminate all physical cash from the global economy
Because bearer instruments are illegal in all FATF member countries
Because cross-border cash transportation is only used by terrorist organizations and never by legitimate travelers

explanation.text: The Logic: FATF cash-courier measures are designed to detect the physical cross-border transportation of currency and bearer negotiable instruments, including restraint or confiscation where such movement is related to ML/TF. Physical banknote movement is one of the main methods for moving value. The Trap: The incorrect options overstate FATF's intent — FATF does not seek to eliminate cash, declare bearer instruments illegal everywhere, or claim that only terrorists move cash across borders. Note: Detection mechanisms (such as declaration systems at borders) target suspicious movements outside the formal financial system.
